# Meeting Room Booking: Feature Specification

## 1. Document Status

- Run ID: 20261013-114601-e40cb7
- Date: 2026-10-13
- Run mode: fixture
- Publication status: pending final pass
- Known limitations: Capture covers one page only (SCR-001) and is a static fixture, so empty, loading, error, confirmation and success states and the behaviour of Book and Cancel booking were not observed, and no screen for the facilities team's blocking workflow was captured. Research is limited to one fixture source that describes itself as not real documentation (low confidence); research for GAP-002 returned no findings. All decisions DEC-001 to DEC-009 come from a pre-written eval case file, not from a live customer. Change 1 (DEC-007, DEC-008) replaced the booking limit and the cancellation rule after the original review; most feasibility items, deferred gaps and the earlier research recommendations became stale and superseded.
- Open stale items: none awaiting reconfirmation (no stale approved items). 26 stale items are all Superseded and appear in the Decisions Log (section 15) and in section 16.
- Unresolved blocking issues: blocking questions Q-001 to Q-006 are unanswered. REQ-003 carries the label Unknown.

## 2. Executive Summary

This feature lets staff book meeting rooms, lets bookings be cancelled by the person who made them or by a room admin, and lets the facilities team (the room admins) block rooms for maintenance.

The customer has decided that staff can book a room for up to 2 hours (DEC-007, replacing the earlier 4-hour limit) and that a booking can be cancelled by its owner or by a room admin (DEC-008, replacing the earlier owner-only rule). The customer also stated that room admins are the facilities team, that a block has a start and end date and time and a reason, that blocks do not repeat, and that a block cancels existing bookings in its period and emails their owners.

Several important behaviours are not yet decided. The most important are: whether two bookings for the same room may overlap and whether a room can be booked during a block (Q-001); whether the facilities team confirms before a block cancels other people's bookings and whether a block can be undone (Q-002); and how a block treats bookings that only partly overlap it (Q-003). The research available is one low-confidence fixture source, now superseded, so no research recommendation is in force.

## 3. Goals and Scope

### Goals

- Let staff reserve a meeting room for up to 2 hours (FR-001).
- Let a booking be cancelled by the person who made it or by a room admin (FR-003).
- Let room admins block rooms for maintenance (FR-006).

### In Scope

- Booking a room through the form seen in the mockup (Room, Start, Duration, Book) and listing the user's own bookings with a Cancel booking action (sections 8 and 12).
- Cancellation by the owner or by a room admin.
- Maintenance blocks created by the facilities team, including cancelling existing bookings in the blocked period and emailing their owners.
- Approved gaps GAP-001, GAP-002, GAP-003, GAP-007, GAP-009, GAP-010, GAP-013 and GAP-014 (reconfirmed by DEC-009). Each is still open and tracked in sections 7 and 16.

### Out of Scope / Rejected

No item carries a Rejected label in this run, so nothing is listed as rejected. No exclusion is inferred from the mockup.

### Deferred

No item has a deferred placement in this run. Gaps that DEC-006 deferred now carry the derived label Superseded and are shown in the Decisions Log (section 15) and in the record tables.

## 4. Users and Roles

- Staff: every employee with a company account (DEC-001). They may book any meeting room (DEC-001) and may cancel their own bookings (DEC-008).
- Visitors and contractors: cannot book (DEC-001). What they see when they reach the page is not defined (Q-005).
- Room admins: the facilities team (DEC-004). They may create maintenance blocks and, under DEC-008, cancel bookings. Unknown: whether they can block every room or only some, and how membership of the team is decided (Q-004).
- Not defined: who maintains the room list (Oak and Elm are shown in the mockup) (Q-010).

## 5. Existing Mockup Coverage

All entries below are Observed in the capture (one page, static fixture, capture status complete).

- SCR-001 (Observed): page "Book a meeting room". Default state only: form with Room "Oak", empty Start, Duration "1 hour", and a "My bookings" table with one row "Oak, 5 Mar 10:00, 2 hours".
- SCR-002 (Observed): booking form with Room (options Oak, Elm), Start (date-time input), Duration (options 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours) and a Book button. No required-field markers are visible. The 4 hours option is longer than the 2-hour limit decided in DEC-007 (OQ-W-001).
- SCR-003 (Observed): "My bookings" table with a Cancel booking button per row.
- SCR-004 (Observed): Booking data entity. Room, Start and Duration are visible; the booker (owner of "My bookings") is inferred, not visible.
- Ambiguous behaviours recorded in the capture: who can book and whether sign-in is required; required fields; past and overlapping times; feedback after Book; time zone and step rules; availability display; editing; confirmation, deadline, restoration and failure on cancel; empty table and past bookings.
- Capture limitations: only one page; empty, loading, error, confirmation and success states not shown; behaviour on Book and Cancel booking not observed; no flows captured.
- ASM-G-001 (Assumption): the captured page is the staff-facing booking view only, and the absence of a facilities blocking screen means it was not captured, not that it does not exist.

## 7. Gaps Identified

| GAP-004 | Two people booking the same slot at the same moment, and repeated Book presses | Superseded: DEC-006 | research | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001 |

| GAP-007 | Cancellation confirmation, start-time cutoff in the list, and what happens to cancelled rows | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Q-008 |
| GAP-008 | Content and delivery failure of the block-cancellation email | Superseded: DEC-006 | both | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-002 |
| GAP-009 | Staff cannot see room availability or maintenance blocks before choosing a time | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Q-007 |
| GAP-010 | Sign-in requirement and bookings of staff who leave or lose access | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Q-005 |
| GAP-011 | Accessibility of the booking form and per-row Cancel booking actions | Superseded: DEC-006 | research | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001, REQ-002 |
| GAP-012 | Time zone and time granularity for Start and blocks | Superseded: DEC-006 | both | optional | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001 |
| GAP-013 | Traceability of blocks and cancellations | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | optional | open (customer decision pending) | Q-009 |
| GAP-014 | Editing bookings, managing the room list, and retention of past bookings | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | optional | open (customer decision pending) | Q-006, Q-010 |

## 8. Functional Requirements

### Booking rooms

Staff reserve a meeting room by choosing a room, a start time and a duration. Behaviour the customer has not decided is listed in section 16 and is not specified here: whether bookings may overlap or be made inside a block (Q-001), what staff see of availability (Q-007), and whether bookings can be edited (Q-010).

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-001** Staff can book a meeting room for up to 2 hours. [Decision: REQ-004 · Decided: DEC-007] [Decision: DEC-007]

#### Requirements resting on assumptions or open questions

These are not confirmed. Each carries its own label and is pending customer confirmation.

- **FR-002** Assumed under ASM-W-001, pending confirmation: booking is limited to staff, meaning every employee with a company account; visitors and contractors cannot book; staff may book any meeting room. The answer DEC-001 was given for the earlier requirement REQ-001 and is carried over to FR-001 only by this assumption. [Assumption: ASM-W-001 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-001]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

None. The earlier research recommendations are Superseded and appear only in the Decisions Log.

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-001** Given a signed-in employee with a company account and no other booking for room Oak at the chosen time, When they book Oak starting 7 days from now for 2 hours, Then a booking owned by that employee is created. The confirmation message shown is not defined. [Decision: REQ-004 · Decided: DEC-007] [Decision: DEC-007]
- **AC-002** Given a signed-in employee, When they submit a booking of exactly 2 hours, Then it is accepted; and When they submit a booking of 3 hours, Then it is refused and no booking is created. ## 11. Data Model and Business Rules

Entities below are taken from the mockup and the customer's answers. No schema or database was inspected, so none is claimed.

- Booking: Room, Start and Duration are visible in the mockup (SCR-004, Observed). The booker (owner) is inferred from "My bookings" and is needed by the ownership rule in FR-003. Maximum duration is 2 hours (DEC-007).
- Block: per DEC-005, a room, a start date and time, an end date and time, and a reason. This is the customer's wording, not an observed form.
- Relationships: a block cancels the bookings in its period (FR-009). Whether it affects only the blocked room is not stated and is not assumed here.
- Not defined: editing of bookings, who maintains the room list, retention of past and cancelled bookings (Q-006, Q-010).

- **BR-001** The 2-hour limit applies to each booking, a booking may start up to 30 days ahead, and recurring bookings are not offered. These came from the answer DEC-002 to the earlier requirement and are carried over. [Assumption: ASM-W-001 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-002]
- **BR-002** Blocks do not repeat. [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]

## 12. Screens and User Flows

- **FR-011** The booking page shows a form with Room (Oak, Elm), Start (date-time input), Duration (1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours) and a Book button. The 4 hours option conflicts with FR-001 and needs a customer answer (OQ-W-001). [Mockup: SCR-002 · Observed]
- **FR-012** The page shows a "My bookings" table listing the user's bookings, each with a Cancel booking button. [Mockup: SCR-003 · Observed]

Booking flow as observed: choose room, start and duration, then press Book. What happens after Book is not shown in the capture. Cancellation flow as observed: press Cancel booking on a row; confirmation, failure and the resulting list are not shown. No screen for room admins to cancel a booking was captured. The facilities team's blocking flow, any availability view and sign-in screens were not captured (ASM-G-001; Q-002, Q-005, Q-007).

## 13. Integrations and Dependencies

- Email: owners of bookings cancelled by a block must be emailed (FR-010). No supplied document establishes how email would be sent or where owners' addresses come from.
- Company accounts: eligibility depends on identifying employees with a company account (FR-002). No supplied document establishes how sign-in or the check works, or how disabled accounts become known (Q-005).
- Room list: Oak and Elm are shown; whether the list comes from an existing source is not established (Q-010).

## 14. Security, Privacy, and Error Handling

- Permissions are defined in FR-002 (who may book, assumed), FR-003 and FR-004 (who may cancel; FR-004 assumed) and FR-007 (who may block); refusal behaviour is covered by AC-003, AC-007 and AC-010.
- Error, empty and loading states, email delivery failure, duplicate submissions and concurrent bookings are not specified; they are open gaps without a decision (section 7).
- Privacy: booking records name the person who booked. How long past and cancelled bookings are kept is undecided (Q-006), and whether staff see other people's names on an availability view is undecided (Q-007).

1	# Meeting Room Booking: Feature Specification
2	
3	## 1. Document Status
4	
5	- Run ID: 20261013-114601-e40cb7
6	- Date: 2026-10-13
7	- Run mode: fixture
8	- Publication status: pending final pass
9	- Known limitations: Capture covers one page only (SCR-001) and is a static fixture, so empty, loading, error, confirmation and success states and the behaviour of Book and Cancel booking were not observed, and no screen for the facilities team's blocking workflow was captured. Research is limited to one fixture source that describes itself as not real documentation (low confidence); research for GAP-002 returned no findings. All decisions DEC-001 to DEC-009 come from a pre-written eval case file, not from a live customer. Change 1 (DEC-007, DEC-008) replaced the booking limit and the cancellation rule after the original review; most feasibility items, deferred gaps and the earlier research recommendations became stale and superseded.
10	- Open stale items: none awaiting reconfirmation (no stale approved items). 26 stale items are all Superseded and appear in the Decisions Log (section 15) and in section 16.
11	- Unresolved blocking issues: blocking questions Q-001 to Q-006 are unanswered. REQ-003 carries the label Unknown.
12	
13	## 2. Executive Summary
14	
15	This feature lets staff book meeting rooms, lets bookings be cancelled by the person who made them or by a room admin, and lets the facilities team (the room admins) block rooms for maintenance.
16	
17	The customer has decided that staff can book a room for up to 2 hours (DEC-007, replacing the earlier 4-hour limit) and that a booking can be cancelled by its owner or by a room admin (DEC-008, replacing the earlier owner-only rule). The customer also stated that room admins are the facilities team, that a block has a start and end date and time and a reason, that blocks do not repeat, and that a block cancels existing bookings in its period and emails their owners.
18	
19	Several important behaviours are not yet decided. The most important are: whether two bookings for the same room may overlap and whether a room can be booked during a block (Q-001); whether the facilities team confirms before a block cancels other people's bookings and whether a block can be undone (Q-002); and how a block treats bookings that only partly overlap it (Q-003). The research available is one low-confidence fixture source, now superseded, so no research recommendation is in force.
20	
21	## 3. Goals and Scope
22	
23	### Goals
24	
25	- Let staff reserve a meeting room for up to 2 hours (FR-001).
26	- Let a booking be cancelled by the person who made it or by a room admin (FR-003).
27	- Let room admins block rooms for maintenance (FR-006).
28	
29	### In Scope
30	
31	- Booking a room through the form seen in the mockup (Room, Start, Duration, Book) and listing the user's own bookings with a Cancel booking action (sections 8 and 12).
32	- Cancellation by the owner or by a room admin.
33	- Maintenance blocks created by the facilities team, including cancelling existing bookings in the blocked period and emailing their owners.
34	- Approved gaps GAP-001, GAP-002, GAP-003, GAP-007, GAP-009, GAP-010, GAP-013 and GAP-014 (reconfirmed by DEC-009). Each is still open and tracked in sections 7 and 16.
35	
36	### Out of Scope / Rejected
37	
38	No item carries a Rejected label in this run, so nothing is listed as rejected. No exclusion is inferred from the mockup.
39	
40	### Deferred
41	
42	No item has a deferred placement in this run. Gaps that DEC-006 deferred now carry the derived label Superseded and are shown in the Decisions Log (section 15) and in the record tables.
43	
44	## 4. Users and Roles
45	
46	- Staff: every employee with a company account (DEC-001). They may book any meeting room (DEC-001) and may cancel their own bookings (DEC-008).
47	- Visitors and contractors: cannot book (DEC-001). What they see when they reach the page is not defined (Q-005).
48	- Room admins: the facilities team (DEC-004). They may create maintenance blocks and, under DEC-008, cancel bookings. Unknown: whether they can block every room or only some, and how membership of the team is decided (Q-004).
49	- Not defined: who maintains the room list (Oak and Elm are shown in the mockup) (Q-010).
50	
51	## 5. Existing Mockup Coverage
52	
53	All entries below are Observed in the capture (one page, static fixture, capture status complete).
54	
55	- SCR-001 (Observed): page "Book a meeting room". Default state only: form with Room "Oak", empty Start, Duration "1 hour", and a "My bookings" table with one row "Oak, 5 Mar 10:00, 2 hours".
56	- SCR-002 (Observed): booking form with Room (options Oak, Elm), Start (date-time input), Duration (options 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours) and a Book button. No required-field markers are visible. The 4 hours option is longer than the 2-hour limit decided in DEC-007 (OQ-W-001).
57	- SCR-003 (Observed): "My bookings" table with a Cancel booking button per row.
58	- SCR-004 (Observed): Booking data entity. Room, Start and Duration are visible; the booker (owner of "My bookings") is inferred, not visible.
59	- Ambiguous behaviours recorded in the capture: who can book and whether sign-in is required; required fields; past and overlapping times; feedback after Book; time zone and step rules; availability display; editing; confirmation, deadline, restoration and failure on cancel; empty table and past bookings.
60	- Capture limitations: only one page; empty, loading, error, confirmation and success states not shown; behaviour on Book and Cancel booking not observed; no flows captured.
61	- ASM-G-001 (Assumption): the captured page is the staff-facing booking view only, and the absence of a facilities blocking screen means it was not captured, not that it does not exist.
62	
63	## 6. Requirements Traceability
64	
65	| REQ | Requirement | Treatment | Label | References |
66	|---|---|---|---|---|
67	| REQ-001 | Staff can book a meeting room for up to 4 hours. | out of scope | Superseded: DEC-007 | Replaced by REQ-004 (DEC-007); see section 15 |
68	| REQ-002 | Bookings can be cancelled by the person who made them. | out of scope | Superseded: DEC-008 | Replaced by REQ-005 (DEC-008); see section 15 |
69	| REQ-003 | Room admins can block rooms for maintenance. | partially addressed | Unknown | DEC-004, DEC-005; FR-006 to FR-010; open: Q-002, Q-003, Q-004 |
70	| REQ-004 | Staff can book a meeting room for up to 2 hours. | addressed | Decided: DEC-007 | DEC-007; FR-001, FR-002, BR-001; open: Q-001, Q-007, OQ-W-001 |
71	| REQ-005 | Bookings can be cancelled by the person who made them or by a room admin. | addressed | Decided: DEC-008 | DEC-008; FR-003 to FR-005; open: OQ-W-002 |
72	
73	## 7. Gaps Identified
74	
75	| GAP | Gap | Approval | Path | Priority | Status | Rationale |
76	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
77	| GAP-001 | Maintenance blocking by room admins is not covered by the mockup | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | critical | open (customer decision pending) | No screen or flow for the facilities workflow was captured (Q-002) |
78	| GAP-002 | Rules for overlapping bookings and bookings that clash with a block are undefined | Approved: DEC-009 | both | critical | open (researched; customer decision pending) | Research returned no findings (OQ-W-003); Q-001 |
79	| GAP-003 | Blocking cancels other people's bookings with no defined safeguard or recovery | Approved: DEC-009 | both | critical | open (researched; customer decision pending) | One low-confidence fixture source, now superseded (OQ-W-004); Q-002 |
80	| GAP-004 | Two people booking the same slot at the same moment, and repeated Book presses | Superseded: DEC-006 | research | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001 |
81	| GAP-005 | Booking form validation and limit enforcement are unspecified | Superseded: DEC-006 | both | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001 |
82	| GAP-006 | Outcome states after Book and Cancel booking, and empty or loading list states, not shown | Superseded: DEC-006 | both | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001, REQ-002 |
83	| GAP-007 | Cancellation confirmation, start-time cutoff in the list, and what happens to cancelled rows | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Q-008 |
84	| GAP-008 | Content and delivery failure of the block-cancellation email | Superseded: DEC-006 | both | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-002 |
85	| GAP-009 | Staff cannot see room availability or maintenance blocks before choosing a time | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Q-007 |
86	| GAP-010 | Sign-in requirement and bookings of staff who leave or lose access | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Q-005 |
87	| GAP-011 | Accessibility of the booking form and per-row Cancel booking actions | Superseded: DEC-006 | research | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001, REQ-002 |
88	| GAP-012 | Time zone and time granularity for Start and blocks | Superseded: DEC-006 | both | optional | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001 |
89	| GAP-013 | Traceability of blocks and cancellations | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | optional | open (customer decision pending) | Q-009 |
90	| GAP-014 | Editing bookings, managing the room list, and retention of past bookings | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | optional | open (customer decision pending) | Q-006, Q-010 |
91	
92	## 8. Functional Requirements
93	
94	### Booking rooms
95	
96	Staff reserve a meeting room by choosing a room, a start time and a duration. Behaviour the customer has not decided is listed in section 16 and is not specified here: whether bookings may overlap or be made inside a block (Q-001), what staff see of availability (Q-007), and whether bookings can be edited (Q-010).
97	
98	#### Confirmed requirements
99	
100	- **FR-001** Staff can book a meeting room for up to 2 hours. [Decision: REQ-004 · Decided: DEC-007] [Decision: DEC-007]
101	
102	#### Requirements resting on assumptions or open questions
103	
104	These are not confirmed. Each carries its own label and is pending customer confirmation.
105	
106	- **FR-002** Assumed under ASM-W-001, pending confirmation: booking is limited to staff, meaning every employee with a company account; visitors and contractors cannot book; staff may book any meeting room. The answer DEC-001 was given for the earlier requirement REQ-001 and is carried over to FR-001 only by this assumption. [Assumption: ASM-W-001 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-001]
107	
108	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
109	
110	None. The earlier research recommendations are Superseded and appear only in the Decisions Log.
111	
112	#### Acceptance criteria
113	
114	- **AC-001** Given a signed-in employee with a company account and no other booking for room Oak at the chosen time, When they book Oak starting 7 days from now for 2 hours, Then a booking owned by that employee is created. The confirmation message shown is not defined. [Decision: REQ-004 · Decided: DEC-007] [Decision: DEC-007]
115	- **AC-002** Given a signed-in employee, When they submit a booking of exactly 2 hours, Then it is accepted; and When they submit a booking of 3 hours, Then it is refused and no booking is created. The wording of the refusal message is not defined. [Decision: REQ-004 · Decided: DEC-007] [Decision: DEC-007]
116	- **AC-003** (draft) Given a visitor, a contractor or a user who is not signed in with a company account, When they attempt to book a room, Then no booking is created. What they see instead is not defined (Q-005). [Assumption: ASM-W-001 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-001]
117	- **AC-004** (draft) Given a signed-in employee, When they submit a 2-hour booking that starts 29 days from now, Then it is accepted; and When they submit one that starts 31 days from now, Then it is refused and no booking is created. The exact boundary day (30 days) and message are not defined. [Assumption: ASM-W-001 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-002]
118	
119	### Cancelling bookings
120	
121	#### Confirmed requirements
122	
123	- **FR-003** Bookings can be cancelled by the person who made them or by a room admin. [Decision: REQ-005 · Decided: DEC-008] [Decision: DEC-008]
124	
125	#### Requirements resting on assumptions or open questions
126	
127	These are not confirmed. Each carries its own label and is pending customer confirmation.
128	
129	- **FR-004** Assumed under ASM-W-002, pending confirmation: anyone who is neither the owner nor a room admin cannot cancel a booking, and an attempt is refused. This is implied by DEC-008 but not stated in it. [Assumption: ASM-W-002 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-008]
130	- **FR-005** Assumed under ASM-W-003, pending confirmation: the owner can cancel a booking only before it starts. This is carried over from the earlier answer DEC-003; whether the same limit applies to room admins is not decided (OQ-W-002). [Assumption: ASM-W-003 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-003]
131	
132	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
133	
134	None for this feature area. Whether cancelling asks for confirmation or can be undone is an open question (Q-008).
135	
136	#### Acceptance criteria
137	
138	- **AC-005** Given a booking owned by Alice that starts in 2 days, When Alice cancels it, Then the booking is cancelled. Whether the room is bookable again immediately and what Alice sees afterwards are not defined (Q-008). [Decision: REQ-005 · Decided: DEC-008] [Decision: DEC-008]
139	- **AC-006** Given a booking owned by Alice and a signed-in member of the facilities team (a room admin), When that member cancels Alice's booking, Then the booking is cancelled. Whether Alice is notified is not defined (OQ-W-002). [Decision: REQ-005 · Decided: DEC-008] [Decision: DEC-008]
140	- **AC-007** (draft) Given a booking owned by Alice, When Bob (an employee who is neither the owner nor a room admin) attempts to cancel it, Then the cancellation is refused and the booking stays active. [Assumption: ASM-W-002 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-008]
141	- **AC-008** (draft) Given a booking owned by Alice that has already started, When Alice attempts to cancel it, Then the cancellation is refused. [Assumption: ASM-W-003 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-003]
142	
143	### Maintenance blocks
144	
145	#### Confirmed requirements
146	
147	- **FR-007** Only room admins, who are the facilities team, may create maintenance blocks. Staff who are not in the facilities team must not be able to block rooms. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
148	- **FR-010** The owner of each booking cancelled by a block must be emailed. The content of the email and how delivery failures are handled are not defined. [Customer: FEA-010 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
149	
150	#### Requirements resting on assumptions or open questions
151	
152	These carry the label Unknown because REQ-003 is not fully decided. They are not confirmed.
153	
154	- **FR-006** Room admins can block rooms for maintenance. The label stays Unknown because which rooms each admin covers, whether a block can be changed or undone, and how partly overlapping bookings are treated are undecided (Q-002, Q-003, Q-004). [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-004]
155	- **FR-008** A block has a start date and time, an end date and time, and a reason. Blocks do not repeat. [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]
156	- **FR-009** Existing bookings in the blocked period are cancelled. Whether a booking that only partly overlaps the period, or is already in progress, is cancelled is not decided (Q-003). [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]
157	
158	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
159	
160	None. The earlier research recommendation on confirming a block is Superseded and appears only in the Decisions Log; the question itself remains open (Q-002).
161	
162	#### Acceptance criteria
163	
164	- **AC-009** (draft) Given a member of the facilities team, When they create a block for room Oak with a start date and time, an end date and time after the start, and a reason, Then the block is recorded for Oak. Whether blocks can be edited or removed is not defined (Q-002). [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]
165	- **AC-010** Given an employee who is not in the facilities team, When they attempt to create a block, Then the attempt is refused and no block is created. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
166	- **AC-011** (draft) Given a member of the facilities team, When they submit a block with no reason, Then the request is refused and no block is created. DEC-005 says a block is made "with a reason"; the refusal wording is not defined. [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]
167	- **AC-012** Given room Oak has an active booking owned by Alice that lies entirely inside the period of a new block, When the facilities team creates the block, Then Alice's booking is cancelled and Alice is emailed. Partly overlapping and in-progress bookings are not covered (Q-003). [Customer: FEA-010 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-003] [Decision: DEC-005]
168	
169	Not specified because the customer has not decided: empty, loading and error states, duplicate submissions, concurrent requests and recovery after failure. These are recorded in section 16 rather than chosen here.
170	
171	## 9. State Transitions and Edge Cases
172	
173	### Booking lifecycle
174	
175	Cancelled, Cancelled (by block) and Past are treated as terminal in this table, except where a row says Unknown. What happens to them afterwards, including whether a cancelled booking returns when a block is removed, is undecided (Q-002, Q-008).
176	
177	| State | Event | Next state | Who can trigger | Provenance |
178	|---|---|---|---|---|
179	| (none) | Staff member submits a valid booking of up to 2 hours | Active | Staff (employee with a company account) | [Decision: REQ-004 · Decided: DEC-007] |
180	| (none) | Booking submitted for a time already held by another booking, or inside a block | Unknown | Unknown | [Inferred: GAP-002 · Approved: DEC-009] |

# Stage 16: Report

Goal: an honest summary, the publication status written into the specification, and the
run closed. §7 Stage 16, §9.14.

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify`, `run_state.py stage 16 --run <run-id> --start`.
2. `run_state.py report --run <run-id>`: merges agent warnings into `warnings.json`, computes the
   publication status (`validated`, `validated_with_warnings`, `not_fully_validated`, `blocked`;
   always `eval_only` in fixture mode) and writes `run_summary.json`.
3. Agent tool, `subagent_type: doc-writer`, `Mode: final`, same run details plus
   `Run summary: <run dir>/run_summary.json`. It rewrites only Document Status.
4. `<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/check_spec.py --run <run-id> --final` (Document Status shows the
   computed status exactly; nothing else changed). If it fails, one more `final` pass, then
   re-check.
5. `run_state.py record-revision --run <run-id> --final`, then
   `run_state.py stage 16 --run <run-id> --complete`, then `run_state.py end --run <run-id>`
   (removes `.active_run`; the session is released).

## Report to the user (in chat)

From `run_summary.json` and the artifacts:

1	# Meeting Room Booking: Feature Specification
2	
3	## 1. Document Status
4	
5	- Run ID: 20261013-114601-e40cb7
6	- Date: 2026-10-13
7	- Run mode: fixture
8	- Publication status: pending final pass
9	- Known limitations: Capture covers one page only (SCR-001) and is a static fixture, so empty, loading, error, confirmation and success states and the behaviour of Book and Cancel booking were not observed, and no screen for the facilities team's blocking workflow was captured. Research is limited to one fixture source that describes itself as not real documentation (low confidence); research for GAP-002 returned no findings. All decisions DEC-001 to DEC-009 come from a pre-written eval case file, not from a live customer. Change 1 (DEC-007, DEC-008) replaced the booking limit and the cancellation rule after the original review; most feasibility items, deferred gaps and the earlier research recommendations became stale and superseded.
10	- Open stale items: none awaiting reconfirmation (no stale approved items). 26 stale items are all Superseded and appear in the Decisions Log (section 15) and in section 16.
11	- Unresolved blocking issues: blocking questions Q-001 to Q-006 are unanswered. REQ-003 carries the label Unknown.
12	
13	## 2. Executive Summary
14	
15	This feature lets staff book meeting rooms, lets bookings be cancelled by the person who made them or by a room admin, and lets the facilities team (the room admins) block rooms for maintenance.
16	
17	The customer has decided that staff can book a room for up to 2 hours (DEC-007, replacing the earlier 4-hour limit) and that a booking can be cancelled by its owner or by a room admin (DEC-008, replacing the earlier owner-only rule). The customer also stated that room admins are the facilities team, that a block has a start and end date and time and a reason, that blocks do not repeat, and that a block cancels existing bookings in its period and emails their owners.
18	
19	Several important behaviours are not yet decided. The most important are: whether two bookings for the same room may overlap and whether a room can be booked during a block (Q-001); whether the facilities team confirms before a block cancels other people's bookings and whether a block can be undone (Q-002); and how a block treats bookings that only partly overlap it (Q-003). The research available is one low-confidence fixture source, now superseded, so no research recommendation is in force.
20	
21	## 3. Goals and Scope
22	
23	### Goals
24	
25	- Let staff reserve a meeting room for up to 2 hours (FR-001).
26	- Let a booking be cancelled by the person who made it or by a room admin (FR-003).
27	- Let room admins block rooms for maintenance (FR-006).
28	
29	### In Scope
30	
31	- Booking a room through the form seen in the mockup (Room, Start, Duration, Book) and listing the user's own bookings with a Cancel booking action (sections 8 and 12).
32	- Cancellation by the owner or by a room admin.
33	- Maintenance blocks created by the facilities team, including cancelling existing bookings in the blocked period and emailing their owners.
34	- Approved gaps GAP-001, GAP-002, GAP-003, GAP-007, GAP-009, GAP-010, GAP-013 and GAP-014 (reconfirmed by DEC-009). Each is still open and tracked in sections 7 and 16.
35	
36	### Out of Scope / Rejected
37	
38	No item carries a Rejected label in this run, so nothing is listed as rejected. No exclusion is inferred from the mockup.
39	
40	### Deferred
41	
42	No item has a deferred placement in this run. Gaps that DEC-006 deferred now carry the derived label Superseded and are shown in the Decisions Log (section 15) and in the record tables.
43	
44	## 4. Users and Roles
45	
46	- Staff: every employee with a company account (DEC-001). They may book any meeting room (DEC-001) and may cancel their own bookings (DEC-008).
47	- Visitors and contractors: cannot book (DEC-001). What they see when they reach the page is not defined (Q-005).
48	- Room admins: the facilities team (DEC-004). They may create maintenance blocks and, under DEC-008, cancel bookings. Unknown: whether they can block every room or only some, and how membership of the team is decided (Q-004).
49	- Not defined: who maintains the room list (Oak and Elm are shown in the mockup) (Q-010).
50	
51	## 5. Existing Mockup Coverage
52	
53	All entries below are Observed in the capture (one page, static fixture, capture status complete).
54	
55	- SCR-001 (Observed): page "Book a meeting room". Default state only: form with Room "Oak", empty Start, Duration "1 hour", and a "My bookings" table with one row "Oak, 5 Mar 10:00, 2 hours".
56	- SCR-002 (Observed): booking form with Room (options Oak, Elm), Start (date-time input), Duration (options 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours) and a Book button. No required-field markers are visible. The 4 hours option is longer than the 2-hour limit decided in DEC-007 (OQ-W-001).
57	- SCR-003 (Observed): "My bookings" table with a Cancel booking button per row.
58	- SCR-004 (Observed): Booking data entity. Room, Start and Duration are visible; the booker (owner of "My bookings") is inferred, not visible.
59	- Ambiguous behaviours recorded in the capture: who can book and whether sign-in is required; required fields; past and overlapping times; feedback after Book; time zone and step rules; availability display; editing; confirmation, deadline, restoration and failure on cancel; empty table and past bookings.
60	- Capture limitations: only one page; empty, loading, error, confirmation and success states not shown; behaviour on Book and Cancel booking not observed; no flows captured.
61	- ASM-G-001 (Assumption): the captured page is the staff-facing booking view only, and the absence of a facilities blocking screen means it was not captured, not that it does not exist.
62	
63	## 6. Requirements Traceability
64	
65	| REQ | Requirement | Treatment | Label | References |
66	|---|---|---|---|---|
67	| REQ-001 | Staff can book a meeting room for up to 4 hours. | out of scope | Superseded: DEC-007 | Replaced by REQ-004 (DEC-007); see section 15 |
68	| REQ-002 | Bookings can be cancelled by the person who made them. | out of scope | Superseded: DEC-008 | Replaced by REQ-005 (DEC-008); see section 15 |
69	| REQ-003 | Room admins can block rooms for maintenance. | partially addressed | Unknown | DEC-004, DEC-005; FR-006 to FR-010; open: Q-002, Q-003, Q-004 |
70	| REQ-004 | Staff can book a meeting room for up to 2 hours. | addressed | Decided: DEC-007 | DEC-007; FR-001, FR-002, BR-001; open: Q-001, Q-007, OQ-W-001 |
71	| REQ-005 | Bookings can be cancelled by the person who made them or by a room admin. | addressed | Decided: DEC-008 | DEC-008; FR-003 to FR-005; open: OQ-W-002 |
72	
73	## 7. Gaps Identified
74	
75	| GAP | Gap | Approval | Path | Priority | Status | Rationale |
76	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
77	| GAP-001 | Maintenance blocking by room admins is not covered by the mockup | Approved: DEC-006 | customer | critical | open (customer decision pending) | No screen or flow for the facilities workflow was captured (Q-002) |
78	| GAP-002 | Rules for overlapping bookings and bookings that clash with a block are undefined | Approved: DEC-009 | both | critical | open (researched; customer decision pending) | Research returned no findings (OQ-W-003); Q-001 |
79	| GAP-003 | Blocking cancels other people's bookings with no defined safeguard or recovery | Approved: DEC-009 | both | critical | open (researched; customer decision pending) | One low-confidence fixture source, now superseded (OQ-W-004); Q-002 |
80	| GAP-004 | Two people booking the same slot at the same moment, and repeated Book presses | Superseded: DEC-006 | research | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001 |
81	| GAP-005 | Booking form validation and limit enforcement are unspecified | Superseded: DEC-006 | both | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001 |
82	| GAP-006 | Outcome states after Book and Cancel booking, and empty or loading list states, not shown | Superseded: DEC-006 | both | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001, REQ-002 |
83	| GAP-007 | Cancellation confirmation, start-time cutoff in the list, and what happens to cancelled rows | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Q-008 |
84	| GAP-008 | Content and delivery failure of the block-cancellation email | Superseded: DEC-006 | both | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-002 |
85	| GAP-009 | Staff cannot see room availability or maintenance blocks before choosing a time | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Q-007 |
86	| GAP-010 | Sign-in requirement and bookings of staff who leave or lose access | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | important | open (customer decision pending) | Q-005 |
87	| GAP-011 | Accessibility of the booking form and per-row Cancel booking actions | Superseded: DEC-006 | research | important | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001, REQ-002 |
88	| GAP-012 | Time zone and time granularity for Start and blocks | Superseded: DEC-006 | both | optional | open (superseded; stale after change 1) | DEC-006 recorded a defer action; stale: depends on changed REQ-001 |
89	| GAP-013 | Traceability of blocks and cancellations | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | optional | open (customer decision pending) | Q-009 |
90	| GAP-014 | Editing bookings, managing the room list, and retention of past bookings | Approved: DEC-009 | customer | optional | open (customer decision pending) | Q-006, Q-010 |
91	
92	## 8. Functional Requirements
93	
94	### Booking rooms
95	
96	Staff reserve a meeting room by choosing a room, a start time and a duration. Behaviour the customer has not decided is listed in section 16 and is not specified here: whether bookings may overlap or be made inside a block (Q-001), what staff see of availability (Q-007), and whether bookings can be edited (Q-010).
97	
98	#### Confirmed requirements
99	
100	- **FR-001** Staff can book a meeting room for up to 2 hours. [Decision: REQ-004 · Decided: DEC-007] [Decision: DEC-007]
101	
102	#### Requirements resting on assumptions or open questions
103	
104	These are not confirmed. Each carries its own label and is pending customer confirmation.
105	
106	- **FR-002** Assumed under ASM-W-001, pending confirmation: booking is limited to staff, meaning every employee with a company account; visitors and contractors cannot book; staff may book any meeting room. The answer DEC-001 was given for the earlier requirement REQ-001 and is carried over to FR-001 only by this assumption. [Assumption: ASM-W-001 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-001]
107	
108	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
109	
110	None. The earlier research recommendations are Superseded and appear only in the Decisions Log.
111	
112	#### Acceptance criteria
113	
114	- **AC-001** Given a signed-in employee with a company account and no other booking for room Oak at the chosen time, When they book Oak starting 7 days from now for 2 hours, Then a booking owned by that employee is created. The confirmation message shown is not defined. [Decision: REQ-004 · Decided: DEC-007] [Decision: DEC-007]
115	- **AC-002** Given a signed-in employee, When they submit a booking of exactly 2 hours, Then it is accepted; and When they submit a booking of 3 hours, Then it is refused and no booking is created. The wording of the refusal message is not defined. [Decision: REQ-004 · Decided: DEC-007] [Decision: DEC-007]
116	- **AC-003** (draft) Given a visitor, a contractor or a user who is not signed in with a company account, When they attempt to book a room, Then no booking is created. What they see instead is not defined (Q-005). [Assumption: ASM-W-001 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-001]
117	- **AC-004** (draft) Given a signed-in employee, When they submit a 2-hour booking that starts 29 days from now, Then it is accepted; and When they submit one that starts 31 days from now, Then it is refused and no booking is created. The exact boundary day (30 days) and message are not defined. [Assumption: ASM-W-001 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-002]
118	
119	### Cancelling bookings
120	
121	#### Confirmed requirements
122	
123	- **FR-003** Bookings can be cancelled by the person who made them or by a room admin. [Decision: REQ-005 · Decided: DEC-008] [Decision: DEC-008]
124	
125	#### Requirements resting on assumptions or open questions
126	
127	These are not confirmed. Each carries its own label and is pending customer confirmation.
128	
129	- **FR-004** Assumed under ASM-W-002, pending confirmation: anyone who is neither the owner nor a room admin cannot cancel a booking, and an attempt is refused. This is implied by DEC-008 but not stated in it. [Assumption: ASM-W-002 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-008]
130	- **FR-005** Assumed under ASM-W-003, pending confirmation: the owner can cancel a booking only before it starts. This is carried over from the earlier answer DEC-003; whether the same limit applies to room admins is not decided (OQ-W-002). [Assumption: ASM-W-003 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-003]
131	
132	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
133	
134	None for this feature area. Whether cancelling asks for confirmation or can be undone is an open question (Q-008).
135	
136	#### Acceptance criteria
137	
138	- **AC-005** Given a booking owned by Alice that starts in 2 days, When Alice cancels it, Then the booking is cancelled. Whether the room is bookable again immediately and what Alice sees afterwards are not defined (Q-008). [Decision: REQ-005 · Decided: DEC-008] [Decision: DEC-008]
139	- **AC-006** Given a booking owned by Alice and a signed-in member of the facilities team (a room admin), When that member cancels Alice's booking, Then the booking is cancelled. Whether Alice is notified is not defined (OQ-W-002). [Decision: REQ-005 · Decided: DEC-008] [Decision: DEC-008]
140	- **AC-007** (draft) Given a booking owned by Alice, When Bob (an employee who is neither the owner nor a room admin) attempts to cancel it, Then the cancellation is refused and the booking stays active. [Assumption: ASM-W-002 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-008]
141	- **AC-008** (draft) Given a booking owned by Alice that has already started, When Alice attempts to cancel it, Then the cancellation is refused. [Assumption: ASM-W-003 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-003]
142	
143	### Maintenance blocks
144	
145	#### Confirmed requirements
146	
147	- **FR-007** Only room admins, who are the facilities team, may create maintenance blocks. Staff who are not in the facilities team must not be able to block rooms. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
148	- **FR-010** The owner of each booking cancelled by a block must be emailed. The content of the email and how delivery failures are handled are not defined. [Customer: FEA-010 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-005]
149	
150	#### Requirements resting on assumptions or open questions
151	
152	These carry the label Unknown because REQ-003 is not fully decided. They are not confirmed.
153	
154	- **FR-006** Room admins can block rooms for maintenance. The label stays Unknown because which rooms each admin covers, whether a block can be changed or undone, and how partly overlapping bookings are treated are undecided (Q-002, Q-003, Q-004). [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-004]
155	- **FR-008** A block has a start date and time, an end date and time, and a reason. Blocks do not repeat. [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]
156	- **FR-009** Existing bookings in the blocked period are cancelled. Whether a booking that only partly overlaps the period, or is already in progress, is cancelled is not decided (Q-003). [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]
157	
158	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
159	
160	None. The earlier research recommendation on confirming a block is Superseded and appears only in the Decisions Log; the question itself remains open (Q-002).
161	
162	#### Acceptance criteria
163	
164	- **AC-009** (draft) Given a member of the facilities team, When they create a block for room Oak with a start date and time, an end date and time after the start, and a reason, Then the block is recorded for Oak. Whether blocks can be edited or removed is not defined (Q-002). [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]
165	- **AC-010** Given an employee who is not in the facilities team, When they attempt to create a block, Then the attempt is refused and no block is created. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
166	- **AC-011** (draft) Given a member of the facilities team, When they submit a block with no reason, Then the request is refused and no block is created. DEC-005 says a block is made "with a reason"; the refusal wording is not defined. [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]

Partly overlapping and in-progress bookings are not covered (Q-003). [Customer: FEA-010 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-003] [Decision: DEC-005]
168	
169	Not specified because the customer has not decided: empty, loading and error states, duplicate submissions, concurrent requests and recovery after failure. These are recorded in section 16 rather than chosen here.
170	
171	## 9. State Transitions and Edge Cases
172	
173	### Booking lifecycle
174	
175	Cancelled, Cancelled (by block) and Past are treated as terminal in this table, except where a row says Unknown. What happens to them afterwards, including whether a cancelled booking returns when a block is removed, is undecided (Q-002, Q-008).
176	
177	| State | Event | Next state | Who can trigger | Provenance |
178	|---|---|---|---|---|
179	| (none) | Staff member submits a valid booking of up to 2 hours | Active | Staff (employee with a company account) | [Decision: REQ-004 · Decided: DEC-007] |
180	| (none) | Booking submitted for a time already held by another booking, or inside a block | Unknown | Unknown | [Inferred: GAP-002 · Approved: DEC-009] |
181	| Active | Owner cancels before the start time | Cancelled (terminal) | The booking owner | [Decision: REQ-005 · Decided: DEC-008] [Assumption: ASM-W-003] |
182	| Active | Room admin cancels | Cancelled (terminal; start-time limit for admins: Unknown) | Room admin (facilities team) | [Decision: REQ-005 · Decided: DEC-008] |
183	| Active | Someone who is neither owner nor room admin attempts to cancel | Active (refused) | Not permitted | [Assumption: ASM-W-002 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-008] |
184	| Active | Owner attempts to cancel after the start | Active (refused) | Not permitted | [Assumption: ASM-W-003 · Assumption] |
185	| Active | Booking end time reached | Past (ended, terminal) | System | [Inferred: GAP-007 · Approved: DEC-009] |
186	| Active | Block created that covers the whole booking | Cancelled (by block) | Facilities team | [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005] |
187	| Active | Block created that partly overlaps the booking, or starts while it is in progress | Unknown | Facilities team | [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] |
188	| Active | Owner's account is disabled | Unknown | Unknown | [Inferred: GAP-010 · Approved: DEC-009] |
189	| Cancelled (by block) | Block is removed or shortened | Unknown (restored or stays cancelled) | Unknown | [Inferred: GAP-003 · Approved: DEC-009] |
190	| Cancelled or Past | Shown in My bookings | Unknown (whether they stay listed, Q-008) | Not applicable | [Inferred: GAP-007 · Approved: DEC-009] |
191	
192	### Block lifecycle
193	
194	| State | Event | Next state | Who can trigger | Provenance |
195	|---|---|---|---|---|
196	| (none) | Facilities team member submits start, end and reason | Active block | Facilities team | [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] |
197	| (none) | Employee outside the facilities team attempts to create a block | No block (refused) | Not permitted | [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] |
198	| (none) | Block would cancel existing bookings | Unknown (whether a confirmation step precedes it) | Facilities team | [Inferred: GAP-003 · Approved: DEC-009] |
199	| Active block | Block edited, removed or undone | Unknown | Unknown | [Inferred: GAP-001 · Approved: DEC-006] |
200	| Active block | Block end time reached | Unknown (no state recorded by the customer) | System | [Inferred: GAP-001 · Approved: DEC-006] |
201	
202	## 10. Non-Functional Requirements
203	
204	No non-functional requirements are stated by the customer, and no evidence supports specific numbers. Accessibility, time zone handling, concurrency and error-state topics are open gaps with no decision (section 7) and are not specified here. No performance, availability or compliance figures are claimed.
205	
206	## 11. Data Model and Business Rules
207	
208	Entities below are taken from the mockup and the customer's answers. No schema or database was inspected, so none is claimed.
209	
210	- Booking: Room, Start and Duration are visible in the mockup (SCR-004, Observed). The booker (owner) is inferred from "My bookings" and is needed by the ownership rule in FR-003. Maximum duration is 2 hours (DEC-007).
211	- Block: per DEC-005, a room, a start date and time, an end date and time, and a reason. This is the customer's wording, not an observed form.
212	- Relationships: a block cancels the bookings in its period (FR-009). Whether it affects only the blocked room is not stated and is not assumed here.
213	- Not defined: editing of bookings, who maintains the room list, retention of past and cancelled bookings (Q-006, Q-010).
214	
215	- **BR-001** The 2-hour limit applies to each booking, a booking may start up to 30 days ahead, and recurring bookings are not offered. These came from the answer DEC-002 to the earlier requirement and are carried over. [Assumption: ASM-W-001 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-002]
216	- **BR-002** Blocks do not repeat. [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-005]
217	
218	## 12. Screens and User Flows
219	
220	- **FR-011** The booking page shows a form with Room (Oak, Elm), Start (date-time input), Duration (1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours) and a Book button. The 4 hours option conflicts with FR-001 and needs a customer answer (OQ-W-001). [Mockup: SCR-002 · Observed]
221	- **FR-012** The page shows a "My bookings" table listing the user's bookings, each with a Cancel booking button. [Mockup: SCR-003 · Observed]
222	
223	Booking flow as observed: choose room, start and duration, then press Book. What happens after Book is not shown in the capture. Cancellation flow as observed: press Cancel booking on a row; confirmation, failure and the resulting list are not shown. No screen for room admins to cancel a booking was captured. The facilities team's blocking flow, any availability view and sign-in screens were not captured (ASM-G-001; Q-002, Q-005, Q-007).
224	
225	## 13. Integrations and Dependencies
226	
227	- Email: owners of bookings cancelled by a block must be emailed (FR-010). No supplied document establishes how email would be sent or where owners' addresses come from.
228	- Company accounts: eligibility depends on identifying employees with a company account (FR-002). No supplied document establishes how sign-in or the check works, or how disabled accounts become known (Q-005).
229	- Room list: Oak and Elm are shown; whether the list comes from an existing source is not established (Q-010).
230	
231	## 14. Security, Privacy, and Error Handling
232

# Meeting Room Booking: Feature Specification

## 1. Document Status

- Run ID: 20261013-114601-e40cb7
- Date: 2026-10-13
- Run mode: fixture
- Publication status: eval_only
- Known limitations: Capture covers one page only (SCR-001) and is a static fixture, so empty, loading, error, confirmation and success states and the behaviour of Book and Cancel booking were not observed, and no screen for the facilities team's blocking workflow was captured. Research is limited to one fixture source that describes itself as not real documentation (low confidence); research for GAP-002 returned no findings. All decisions DEC-001 to DEC-009 come from a pre-written eval case file, not from a live customer. Change 1 (DEC-007, DEC-008) replaced the booking limit and the cancellation rule after the original review; most feasibility items, deferred gaps and the earlier research recommendations became stale and superseded.
- Open stale items: none awaiting reconfirmation (no stale approved items). 26 stale items are all Superseded and appear in the Decisions Log (section 15) and in section 16.
- Unresolved blocking issues: the review reports no unresolved issues. Outstanding decisions are Q-001 to Q-010, all unanswered; Q-001 to Q-006 are marked blocking. REQ-003 carries the label Unknown.

## 2. Executive Summary

This feature lets staff book meeting rooms, lets bookings be cancelled by the person who made them or by a room admin, and lets the facilities team (the room admins) block rooms for maintenance.

The customer has decided that staff can book a room for up to 2 hours (DEC-007, replacing the earlier 4-hour limit) and that a booking can be cancelled by its owner or by a room admin (DEC-008, replacing the earlier owner-only rule). The customer also stated that room admins are the facilities team, that a block has a start and end date and time and a reason, that blocks do not repeat, and that a block cancels existing bookings in its period and emails their owners.

Several important behaviours are not yet decided. The most important are: whether two bookings for the same room may overlap and whether a room can be booked during a block (Q-001); whether the facilities team confirms before a block cancels other people's bookings and whether a block can be undone (Q-002); and how a block treats bookings that only partly overlap it (Q-003). The research available is one low-confidence fixture source, now superseded, so no research recommendation is in force.

## 3. Goals and Scope

### Goals

- Let staff reserve a meeting room for up to 2 hours (FR-001).
- Let a booking be cancelled by the person who made it or by a room admin (FR-003).
- Let room admins block rooms for maintenance (FR-006).

### In Scope

- Booking a room through the form seen in the mockup (Room, Start, Duration, Book) and listing the user's own bookings with a Cancel booking action (sections 8 and 12).
- Cancellation by the owner or by a room admin.
- Maintenance blocks created by the facilities team, including cancelling existing bookings in the blocked period and emailing their owners.
- Approved gaps GAP-001, GAP-002, GAP-003, GAP-007, GAP-009, GAP-010, GAP-013 and GAP-014 (reconfirmed by DEC-009). Each is still open and tracked in sections 7 and 16.

### Out of Scope / Rejected

No item carries a Rejected label in this run, so nothing is listed as rejected. No exclusion is inferred from the mockup.

### Deferred

No item has a deferred placement in this run. Gaps that DEC-006 deferred now carry the derived label Superseded and are shown in the Decisions Log (section 15) and in the record tables.

## 4. Users and Roles

- Staff: every employee with a company account (DEC-001). They may book any meeting room (DEC-001) and may cancel their own bookings (DEC-008).
- Visitors and contractors: cannot book (DEC-001). What they see when they reach the page is not defined (Q-005).

Behaviour the customer has not decided is listed in section 16 and is not specified here: whether bookings may overlap or be made inside a block (Q-001), what staff see of availability (Q-007), and whether bookings can be edited (Q-010).

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-001** Staff can book a meeting room for up to 2 hours. [Decision: REQ-004 · Decided: DEC-007] [Decision: DEC-007]

#### Requirements resting on assumptions or open questions

These are not confirmed. Each carries its own label and is pending customer confirmation.

- **FR-002** Assumed under ASM-W-001, pending confirmation: booking is limited to staff, meaning every employee with a company account; visitors and contractors cannot book; staff may book any meeting room. The answer DEC-001 was given for the earlier requirement REQ-001 and is carried over to FR-001 only by this assumption. [Assumption: ASM-W-001 · Assumption] [Decision: DEC-001]

## 14. Security, Privacy, and Error Handling

- Permissions are defined in FR-002 (who may book, assumed), FR-003 and FR-004 (who may cancel; FR-004 assumed) and FR-007 (who may block); refusal behaviour is covered by AC-003, AC-007 and AC-010.

- Privacy: booking records name the person who booked. How long past and cancelled bookings are kept is undecided (Q-006), and whether staff see other people's names on an availability view is undecided (Q-007).
